chunks: A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid Shaynula, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (عليه السلام): 'May I be made your ransom! Indeed our elders narrated from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and the taqiyyah was intense, so they concealed their books and did not narrate from them. When they died, the books came to us.'
So he (عليه السلام) said: 'Narrate from them, for indeed they are true.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: taqiyyah — precautionary dissimulation of faith practiced under threat of Abbasid persecution
key_terms.الْكُتُبُ: the books — written compilations of hadith transmitted from the Imams, hidden to protect their contents
key_terms.حَقٌّ: truth/true — the Imam's authenticating declaration that the texts of these books are valid
key_terms.مَشَايِخَنَا: our elders/sheikhs — senior Shia scholars of the preceding generation who personally received teachings from the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (عليه السلام) say about books of hadith that were concealed during taqiyyah and later passed to the next generation?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct exchange between a companion and Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (عليه السلام), the ninth Imam, concerning books of hadith compiled from Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (عليهم السلام) that had been hidden during the intense taqiyyah of the Abbasid era and subsequently inherited by a later generation of Shia scholars. The Imam (عليه السلام) responds with an unambiguous directive — 'Narrate from them, for indeed they are true' — thereby personally authenticating these concealed written collections and authorizing their public circulation. This narration is foundational in Shia hadith sciences as an Imamic endorsement of the reliability of early written Shia literature.
